description.value: A pilot fMRI study examining relationships between subclinical depressive symptom severity and brain activation during emotion regulation and reward processing, and functional connectivity during rest, in women without major depressive disorder.

spans.text: The goal of the present pilot study was to investigate linkages between regional brain activation patterns and subclinical depressive symptoms while participants were engaged in emotion regulation, resting state, and reward processing paradigms

value: we hypothesized relations between subclinical depressive symptom severity and (1) lateral prefrontal cortex activity during ER; (2) precuneus-dorsolateral prefrontal cortex connectivity during the resting state scan; (3) lateral prefrontal cortex activity during reward selection; (4) striatal activity during reward anticipation; and (5) medial prefrontal cortex activity during reward outcomes.

Emotion Regulation (ER) task

description.value: Participants viewed sad or neutral images and were instructed to reappraise, distract, or view them.

spans.text: During scanning, participants completed the three paradigms described below in a single scan session.
reappraise
Sad images were presented on 75% of trials and were accompanied by an instruction to “reappraise,” “distract,” or “view” the image.

description.value: Participants viewed sad images and were instructed to reappraise their interpretations by giving the depicted story a happy ending or alternate meaning, or by telling themselves that nobody close to them was affected.

spans.text: For the reappraise condition, participants were trained to either give the story suggested in the picture a happy ending or alternate meaning, or to tell themselves that no one close to them was affected by the depicted situation.
view
As a control strategy, participants were instructed to experience the image as they normally would without trying to increase or decrease their emotional response (the “view” condition).

description.value: Participants viewed sad images and were instructed to experience the image as they normally would without trying to increase or decrease their emotional response.

spans.text: As a control strategy, participants were instructed to experience the image as they normally would without trying to increase or decrease their emotional response (the “view” condition).
distract
Sad images were presented on 75% of trials and were accompanied by an instruction to “reappraise,” “distract,” or “view” the image.

description.value: Participants viewed sad images and were instructed to distract themselves by thinking of something positive unrelated to the depicted content, such as a fond memory, family member, or anticipated event.

spans.text: For the distract condition, participants were trained to think of something positive that was unrelated to what was depicted in the images, such as a fond memory, family member, or an anticipated event.
The ER task consisted of four 4-minute 24-second runs with nine sad trials and three neutral trials each
Images were presented using ePrime (Psychology Software Tools Inc., Pittsburgh, PA) for the WOF task, and with CIGAL [ 36 ] for the ER task.
The stimuli used in the task are described elsewhere [ 33 , 34 ].
participants reported their ER success on a 4-point scale

instructions.value: Participants viewed sad or neutral images. For sad images they were instructed to reappraise, distract, or view the image; for neutral images they were instructed to view it. Reappraisal involved giving the depicted story a happy ending or alternate meaning, or telling themselves that nobody close to them was affected. Distraction involved thinking of something positive unrelated to the image. Viewing involved experiencing the image normally without trying to change the emotional response.

value: Self-reported emotion-regulation success on a 4-point scale from not successful to very successful

description.value: A reward-processing task with selection, anticipation, and outcome phases, including monetary and control trials.

spans.text: Briefly, three 12-minute runs with 46 trials each were composed of selection, anticipation, and outcome phases
selection
During the selection phase (3 seconds), participants viewed a segmented wheel of fortune and indicated their selection.
